title: Minimum Cost Path with Edge Reversals
summary: Given a directed, weighted graph with nodes labeled from 0 to n-1 and edges with associated costs, you can reverse an incoming edge at any node exactly once to travel on it, incurring a cost of 2 * wi for that move.
statement: Given a directed, weighted graph with nodes labeled from 0 to n-1 and edges with associated costs, you can reverse an incoming edge at any node exactly once to travel on it, incurring a cost of 2 * wi for that move. Determine the minimum total cost to travel from node 0 to node n-1. If such a path does not exist, return -1.
constraints: Two to 50,000 vertices and up to 100,000 positive weighted directed edges.
Traverse a forward edge for w or reverse an incoming edge for a single move at cost 2w.
Return negative one when the destination is unreachable.
hints: A positive-cost shortest path never needs to revisit a node, so its one-use switch cannot be reused.
Represent each original edge u->v,w by u->v,w and the one-move reversal v->u,2w.
Run Dijkstra from zero in the augmented directed graph.
Every legal move is an augmented edge, and every shortest augmented path is simple and therefore respects the per-node switch restriction.
editorial: Every legal move is an augmented edge, and every shortest augmented path is simple and therefore respects the per-node switch restriction.
